definitions.explanation: Wind blowing in the same direction one is traveling, making movement easier.
Figuratively, circumstances that help or promote progress toward a goal.

examples.japanese: {追|お}い{風|かぜ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けて→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧⟦{船|ふね}→船：00775_fune⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}む→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: The ship moves forward with the tailwind.

examples.japanese: ⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧{追|お}い{風|かぜ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おかげ→おかげ：01362_okage⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: A record was set thanks to a strong tailwind.

examples.english: In track sprints, if the tailwind exceeds two meters per second, the record is not officially recognized.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{追|お}い→追う：02016_ou⟧ (chasing, following) + ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧ (wind). Antonym: ⟦{向|む}かい{風|かぜ}→向かい風：16322_mukaikaze⟧ (headwind; adversity).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {追|お}い{風|かぜ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧ (to catch a tailwind; to benefit from favorable conditions)
- {追|お}い{風|かぜ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become a tailwind/advantage)
- {追|お}い{風|かぜ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ (to ride a tailwind)

USAGE:
The figurative sense is very common in business and economic reporting. {追|お}い{風|かぜ} and ⟦{向|む}かい{風|かぜ}→向かい風：16322_mukaikaze⟧ are frequently paired as metaphors for favorable and unfavorable conditions.
